site.name: aeroiq
site.summary: AeroIQ Fictional API monitoring and observability SaaS (Datadog / Vercel Observability-style). Pages - `index.html` — Overview dashboard. Left rail nav; top bar with org switcher, environment tabs (Production / Staging / Dev), time range (5m / 1h / 24h / 7d), search (⌘K), theme toggle, alert bell; four top KPIs (total requests / error rate / p95 / availability) with sparklines and period-over-period deltas; 24-card endpoint health grid (red cards first), each card with HTTP method + path + health dot + RPS / p95 / error rate; right alerts side panel with 8 active alerts and per-row assign / silence actions; bottom global p50 / p95 / p99 trend line chart. - `endpoint-detail.html` — Endpoint detail. Top: method + path + health badge + linked services + owner avatars; 6 KPIs (RPS / error rate / p50 / p95 / p99 / SLO status); three large trend charts (request volume, latency p50/p95/p99 three lines, error rate); error-grouping panel with status-code / client-version / region tabs; recent error sample table (5 rows including 502 Bad Gateway, 500, 429, 503); related traces list. - `alerts.html` — Alerts center. 4 KPIs (active / new today / mean response / MTTR); filter bar; 12-row alert

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full aeroiq system, prioritizing the primary dashboard flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: AeroIQ offers a visually dense, Datadog-style observability interface, but the current implementation lacks critical functionality and responsiveness. While the core dashboard and endpoint data render well on desktop, the application is severely degraded on mobile viewports due to a rigid, uncollapsible sidebar and overflowing data tables. Additionally, primary interaction paths—such as global search, data context filtering (time/environment), and post-action feedback—are either unresponsive or completely missing, preventing users from effectively analyzing simulated incidents.

exploration_plan.goal: Thoroughly explore the AeroIQ dashboard ecosystem, validating global state controls, drilling down into endpoint details, exercising table filters, and ensuring a robust mobile experience.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will begin on the main dashboard to verify global context switchers (environment, time range) and quick actions like silencing alerts. It will then drill into a specific endpoint's details to interact with data breakdowns. Next, it will cover the list pages (Alerts, Endpoints) to extensively test sorting and filtering mechanisms. The run will conclude with a mobile viewport pass to check the responsiveness of complex data grids and validate flagged small tap targets.
assumptions: Navigational links for Logs, Integrations, and Settings are likely placeholders (href='#') based on prescan.
The ⌘K search input triggers a modal dialog or expanded search state.
Data grids and charts are the primary content, meaning viewport responsiveness is critical for usability.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets on top-bar environment and time-range buttons (mobile risk).
Accessibility of select dropdowns (missing labels reported).
Horizontal scrolling or layout breakage on mobile for wide tables in Alerts and Endpoints.
Interaction state of 'Assign' and 'Silence' buttons on the dashboard alerts panel.

phases.title: Dashboard & Global Controls
phases.objective: Verify the main dashboard layout, global context switchers, and inline alert actions.
key_checks: Toggle between environments (Production, Staging, Dev) and time ranges (5m, 1h, 24h, 7d).
Click 'Assign' or 'Silence' on an active alert in the right panel and observe state changes.
Click the ⌘K search input to verify if a search modal appears.
exit_criteria: Global controls have been clicked and any resulting state changes observed.
Alert action buttons have been exercised.

phases.title: Endpoint Drill-down
phases.objective: Navigate to and explore the detailed view of a specific unhealthy endpoint.
key_checks: Click on a red (unhealthy) endpoint card from the dashboard grid.
On the detail page, switch between the 'By status code', 'By client version', and 'By region' tabs in the Error breakdown section.
Verify the presence of related traces and recent error samples.
exit_criteria: All tabs in the error breakdown section have been clicked and content verified.

phases.title: List Pages & Filtering
phases.objective: Test the complex filtering and search capabilities on the Alerts and Endpoints pages.
key_checks: Navigate to Endpoints page and use the 'All services', 'All health', and 'tag: any' dropdowns.
Type a query into the 'Search method or path...' input on the Endpoints page.
Navigate to Alerts page and exercise the severity, rule, assignee, and status dropdown filters.
exit_criteria: Multiple filter combinations applied and search inputs tested on both pages.

phases.title: Service Map Validation
phases.objective: Check the interactive service topology visualization.
key_checks: Toggle between Production and Staging views on this specific page.
Attempt to click a service node (e.g., 'checkout-api') to see if details load as instructed by the page text.
exit_criteria: Service map page loaded and interaction with nodes/toggles attempted.

phases.title: Mobile Responsive Audit
phases.objective: Re-evaluate critical paths and layouts on a mobile viewport.
key_checks: Verify navigation menu behavior (e.g., hamburger menu).
Check usability of the small tap target top-bar buttons (Time range, Env).
Inspect the Endpoints list table to ensure it doesn't break the horizontal viewport.
Check how the side-by-side charts on the endpoint detail page stack on mobile.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout verified for the dashboard, a list page, and a detail page.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 5 distinct HTML pages identified in the prescan.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise filtering dropdowns, global state toggles, inline alert actions, and tabbed content.
coverage_targets.mobile: Ensure data-dense tables and charts are usable on small screens and tap targets are accessible.

notes: Watch for form submission behaviors on search inputs—they may filter inline via JS or trigger a page reload.
Missing labels on select dropdowns are a known issue; document how this impacts usage, especially if using screen reader emulation or keyboard navigation.

findings.user_goal: Monitor system health and view endpoint metrics on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The application exhibits severe horizontal overflow on mobile screens. The left navigation sidebar does not collapse, and data tables extend far beyond the viewport width.
findings.evidence: Final observation screenshot and layout warnings show the Endpoints page width is 1041px on a 390px viewport, cutting off essential columns like RPS and Error %. Chunks 61-66 and 73-78 confirm this issue exists across the Dashboard, Alerts, and Endpoint Detail pages.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users cannot view crucial metric data or comfortably navigate the application without awkward, forced horizontal scrolling, making on-the-go incident response extremely difficult.
findings.suggestion: Implement a responsive layout: collapse the left sidebar behind a hamburger menu on small screens, and wrap data tables in a horizontally scrollable container (`overflow-x: auto`) or switch to a stacked card layout for mobile.

findings.user_goal: Quickly locate specific endpoints, services, or alerts using search.
findings.problem: The global '⌘K Search...' input provides no live feedback, autocomplete suggestions, or page navigation when text is typed or submitted.
findings.evidence: Chunks 01-06, 31-36, and 61-66 note that typing queries like 'checkout' or 'payments' into the search input produces no dropdown, modal, or filtering results.
findings.why_it_matters: Global search is a primary navigation paradigm for complex observability tools. Without it, users must manually hunt through large lists to find the specific component they are investigating.
findings.suggestion: Implement live search functionality that opens a dropdown menu displaying matching services, endpoints, and alerts as the user types.

findings.user_goal: Filter dashboard metrics by time range and environment to isolate issues.
findings.problem: Context filters such as Time Range (5m, 24h, 7d) and Environment (Staging, Dev) visually update their active button state but fail to change the underlying chart data or KPI metrics.
findings.evidence: Chunks 01-06, 49-54, and 55-60 document clicking these filters and explicitly note that charts remain fixed at '1h' and dashboard data does not refresh.
findings.why_it_matters: Users are locked into a static, default view (e.g., 1-hour production data) and cannot adjust the timeframe or environment to correlate spikes or verify fixes.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the filter toggle events are wired to fetch and update the corresponding metric datasets. If alternative timeframes are not yet implemented, disable the controls and add a 'Coming Soon' tooltip.

findings.user_goal: Silence or assign an active alert and confirm the action was successful.
findings.problem: When confirming an action within a modal dialog (like silencing an alert), the modal dismisses but the system provides no visual feedback or state change to indicate success.
findings.evidence: Chunks 01-06 and 25-30 state that clicking 'Confirm' dismisses the modal, but no toast notification appears, the alert count remains unchanged, and the row button still reads 'Silence' or 'Assign'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users are left uncertain whether their critical operational action actually succeeded, leading to repeated actions and eroding trust in the platform's reliability.
findings.suggestion: Trigger a brief success toast notification upon modal confirmation and optimistically update the UI (e.g., change the 'Silence' button text to 'Silenced' and dim the row).

findings.user_goal: Use a screen reader to filter data tables and switch organizations.
findings.problem: Multiple crucial dropdown selectors (Organization switcher, Services, Health, Severities) lack accessible labels or aria-labels.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in the final observation and across chunks (13-18, 37-42) flag 'missing_input_label' for `<select>` elements like 'Acme Cloud Org' (ux-9) and 'All services' (ux-12).
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will navigate to these form controls and hear them announced as generic dropdowns without context regarding what data attribute they control.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit `<label>` elements associated via the `for` attribute, or apply descriptive `aria-label` attributes directly to all `<select>` elements.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the application menus on a touch device.
findings.problem: Interactive elements, including sidebar navigation links and top-bar profile icons, have interaction areas that are too small for comfortable touch input.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in the final mobile observation list multiple tap targets (e.g., 'Dashboard', 'Endpoints', profile icon) sizing between 34x34px and 39x52px, which are below standard touch guidelines.
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized touch targets increase the likelihood of fat-finger errors and navigation frustration, especially during stressful, time-sensitive incident response.
findings.suggestion: Increase padding to ensure all interactive elements have a minimum tap target size of 44x44px, particularly when rendered on mobile viewports.

findings.user_goal: Visually scan and identify sidebar navigation sections.
findings.problem: Icons in the left navigation menu are rendering as missing character glyphs (empty rectangles) on the page.
findings.evidence: Chunk 31-36 notes 'Left navigation icons... are rendering as missing character glyphs'. The final screenshot shows unrendered vertical rectangles next to the sidebar text (e.g., next to Alerts, Service Map).
findings.why_it_matters: Broken iconography degrades the visual polish and perceived quality of the tool, and removes visual anchors that help users quickly scan the navigation.
findings.suggestion: Verify that the required icon font is correctly loading via CSS, or replace character-based icons with inline SVGs for better cross-platform reliability.

gaps: Only directly exercised 67% of visible interactive feature signatures.
43% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
